The error `/bin/bash: C:/Users/.../script.sh: No such file or directory` is a classic symptom of Windows CRLF (Carriage Return Line Feed) line endings being passed to a Linux-style bash interpreter. Bash sees the `\r` at the end of the shebang line (`#!/bin/bash\r`) and tries to find an interpreter named `/bin/bash\r`, which does not exist. 

To fix this, I will ensure the script is written in a way that minimizes dependencies on specific shell features that might trigger this, and I will provide the code in a clean format. Bash reads `#!/bin/bash\r` and looks for a binary named `bash\r`, which doesn't exist.
